validity.recommendation: no action needed on existence/classification/duplicate; this is the well-documented TAPI megaproject, correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk, and not a duplicate of any other roster row
validity.researcher_notes: This row is the TAPI (Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India) pipeline, one of the most heavily and independently documented gas megaprojects in the world -- ADB (project financier/facilitator), the Turkmenistan and Afghan foreign/mining ministries, Asian Development Bank project pages, Oil & Gas Journal, Eurasianet, World Pipelines, and dozens of press outlets all track it under this exact name and route, entirely independent of GEM. Existence is not in doubt. Classification (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) is correct -- it is explicitly an international gas-export trunk line, not a gathering/feeder line. Checked against the 6-pipeline roster for this batch: P0452 (Iran-Pakistan Pipeline) is a wholly separate project (different supply source -- South Pars, Iran -- different route, different sponsors) and none of the other 4 rows (P3101 Pakistan Stream, P3173 Somiani-Nawabshah, P3174 Off-Shore, P3178 Sawan-Lahore) describe the same corridor or endpoints as TAPI, so no duplicate/relabel concern. Spec values LengthKnown=1814 km, Diameter=56 in, and Capacity=33 bcm/y are all independently corroborated by multiple non-GEM sources (Offshore Technology project page, Wikipedia TAPI Pipeline article, NS Energy Business project page) -- no material disagreement found on those three. CAVEAT: SegmentCost=$7,000,000,000 USD sits inside a genuinely volatile literature -- ADB's original 2005 estimate was $7.6bn, it later blew out toward $10bn, was reportedly cut ~30% to $7bn in Nov 2018, and a 2020 estimate cited $7.7bn; but two independently-sourced, more recent overview pages (Oil & Gas Journal's retrospective and NS Energy Business's project profile) both currently state the cost as $10bn, not $7bn. That is a real, material (~40%) disagreement between GEM's figure and the currently-cited figure in reputable secondary sources, so I did NOT add a ref for SegmentCost as a confirmation -- see the paired validity/spec concern below and the UNRESOLVED fill entry.

validity.recommendation: correct StartState/Province from 'Ahal' to 'Mary' (the Turkmenistan-side origin/border-crossing point and the Galkynysh gas field itself are both in Mary Province, not Ahal Province)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Location [ref] cluster records StartCountryOrArea=Turkmenistan / StartState/Province=Ahal. This is wrong. Four independent sources place both the Galkynysh gas field (the pipeline's stated FuelSource, itself correct) and Serhetabat -- the actual Turkmenistan border town/pipeline crossing point into Afghanistan -- in Mary Province (velayat), not Ahal Province: (1) Wikipedia's Galkynysh Gas Field article states the field is 'near Yoloten in Mary Province of Turkmenistan'; (2) Wikipedia's Serhetabat article states it 'is a city in Tagtabazar District, Mary Province, Turkmenistan ... bordering Afghanistan'; (3) Offshore Technology's TAPI project page states the pipeline 'begins in the Mary region of Turkmenistan'; (4) Turkmenistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs news release on the pipeline's construction launch states it explicitly: 'On 11 September 2024, in the Mary province ... the construction of a key segment of the TAPI pipeline -- the Serhetabat-Herat section ... was launched.' Ahal Province is the central Turkmenistan province around the capital Ashgabat, geographically distinct from Mary Province in the southeast where the field and the border crossing actually sit. EndLocation/EndState-Province/EndCountryOrArea (Fazilka, Punjab, India) are independently confirmed correct by the same Offshore Technology page and by Wikipedia's TAPI Pipeline article, so only the start province needs correction.

validity.recommendation: flag SegmentCost=$7,000,000,000 for review -- currently-cited overview sources say $10bn; do not silently overwrite, the cost figure has genuinely moved across multiple published estimates over 20 years
validity.researcher_notes: See the caveat noted in the first validity entry. Oil & Gas Journal's TAPI retrospective states plainly that 'persistent delays have since raised TAPI's projected cost to $10 billion' (up from ADB's 2005 estimate of $7.6bn, itself up from a 2002 estimate of $2.6bn), and NS Energy Business's project profile independently lists 'Estimated Investment: $10bn.' Those are two independent, reasonably current sources that disagree with GEM's $7bn figure by a material margin. There IS a documented $7bn figure in the literature (a Nov 2018 announcement that project costs were cut ~30% to $7bn, with a 2020 estimate of $7.7bn), so GEM's number is not fabricated or baseless -- it likely reflects that 2018/2020 vintage -- but given more recent sources cite $10bn, I'm flagging this as a genuine spec disagreement rather than confirming or silently filling it. Left SegmentCost unresolved rather than proposing a value change (a real research judgment call, not mechanical).

fills.primary_value: Galkynysh Gas Field (formerly known as Iolotan gas field or South Yolotan – Osman field)
fills.researcher_notes: Wikipedia's Galkynysh Gas Field article confirms it is 'formerly known as Iolotan gas field or South Yolotan-Osman field' -- exact match to GEM's value, including the former-name parenthetical. Offshore Technology's TAPI project page independently confirms gas originates from 'the Galkynysh gas field in Turkmenistan.'

Offshore Technology's TAPI project page states the pipeline 'measures 1,814km in total length.' Wikipedia's TAPI Pipeline article independently states the same 1,814 km figure. Consistent with the sub-segment breakdown reported elsewhere (Turkmenistan ~214km, Afghanistan 774km, Pakistan 826km) summing to ~1,814km.
Offshore Technology states 'a diameter of 56in' (approx. 1,420mm). Wikipedia's TAPI Pipeline article independently confirms the same 56-inch diameter.

Offshore Technology states the system will initially transport 27 bcm/y, 'increasing to 33 billion cubic meters of gas a year' after the first operational year -- 33 bcm/y is the design/full capacity, matching GEM's value. Wikipedia's TAPI Pipeline article independently states the same full design capacity of 33 bcm/year.

This is a CORRECTION, not a plain fill: current sheet value StartState/Province='Ahal' is wrong per the paired attribution-concern validity entry above -- corrected to 'Mary' Province, the province containing both the Galkynysh gas field and the Serhetabat border crossing where TAPI construction actually starts on the Turkmenistan side. EndLocation/EndState-Province/EndCountryOrArea (Fazilka, Punjab, India) were already correct and are re-confirmed here by Offshore Technology's project page and Wikipedia's TAPI Pipeline article ('terminates in Fazilka at the Indo-Pakistan border in Punjab region, India').

Both sources independently confirm the TAPI Pipeline Company Limited (TPCL) shareholding structure agreed under the April 2016 Investment Agreement: Turkmengaz (via its wholly-owned SPV Galkynysh Pipeline Company) 85%, Afghan Gas Enterprise 5%, Inter State Gas Systems (Pakistan) 5%, GAIL (India) 5% -- exact match to GEM's four owners/percentages. Afghanistan's Ministry of Mines TAPI project page (momp.gov.af) also names all four owners (without percentages), a third corroborating source for the ownership identities.

The Inter-Governmental Agreement (IGA) and Gas Pipeline Framework Agreement (GPFA) for TAPI were signed 11 December 2010 in Ashgabat by the heads of state/ministers of Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India -- the contemporaneous 2010-12-13 GlobalSecurity.org wire item and the Offshore Technology project page both date this founding agreement to December 2010, matching GEM's ProposalYear=2010.

Left unresolved rather than confirmed or changed -- see the paired 'spec' concern in validity[]. GEM's $7,000,000,000 figure is plausible (matches a Nov 2018 cost-cut announcement and a 2020 $7.7bn estimate) but two independent, apparently more current overview sources (Oil & Gas Journal, NS Energy Business) currently state $10bn. Deciding which figure is 'current' is a research judgment, not a mechanical fill, so I'm flagging it for the researcher/QC leg rather than proposing a value change myself.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=construction is still correct and remains actively evidenced, not stale. Chronology of dated, independent evidence: (1) 11 September 2024 -- ground broken on the Serhetabat(Turkmenistan)-Herat(Afghanistan) section, 'Arkadagyn ak yoly', the segment GEM's existing ConstructionYear=2024/ConstructionMonth=9 ref (worldpipelines.com) already covers; (2) 20 October 2025 -- Turkmenistan's Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov led a ceremony marking further progress on this 153km section, with Eurasianet and Times of Central Asia both independently reporting roughly 14km of pipe physically laid inside Afghanistan by that date; (3) 3 August 2026 (Ariana News, four days before this review) -- reports that Turkmenistan's government energy review for the first seven months of 2026 gave 'particular attention' to the Serhetabat-Herat section and stated 'work is being carried out in line with international standards.' No evidence found that construction has reached the Pakistan or India segments (per Jamestown and other analyses, those legs remain stalled pending India/Pakistan commercial and security decisions) -- this row is un-segmented (single sheet row for the whole international pipeline) so 'construction' correctly reflects that active, physical construction is genuinely underway on part of the line as of within the last week, even though the Pakistan/India legs have not broken ground. Recommend GEM consider whether this project would be better tracked with country-level segments (as it partly already is for the Iran-Pakistan comparator row), but that is a structural suggestion, not a status error.

summary: TAPI (P0766) is confirmed real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate -- length/diameter/capacity/owners/fuel-source/proposal-year all independently corroborated and refs added; StartState/Province is wrong (Ahal -> should be Mary, corrected) and SegmentCost is a genuine spec disagreement ($7bn on the sheet vs. $10bn in current overview sources, left UNRESOLVED); Status=construction reconfirmed current through an August 2026 Turkmen government statement.
